newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK university allows display of democracy sculptur.
newsitem.headline: HK university allows display of democracy sculptur.

text.p: A Hong Kong university overturned an earlier ban and agreed on Friday to allow its students to display on campus a sculpture symbolising oppression, a student leader said.
The management of the University of Hong Kong made the decision on the "Pillar of Shame" monument after an hour-long meeting with students, their leader Patrick Wong told Reuters.

On Thursday, students and democracy activists took the sculpture onto campus without the permission of the university, which had said its display would be dangerous to students in view of its weight and height.
The sculpture, a grey tower of twisted human bodies depicting oppression by Danish artist Jens Galschiot, is eight metres (26 feet) tall and weighs two tonnes.
There had been speculation that the university had made its earlier decision to avoid upsetting Beijing, which might be offended by the "fight for freedom" monument.
China regains the British colony of 156 years on July 1.
Wong said the university had now accepted the sculpture would pose no danger.
Vice-chancellor Cheng Yiu-chung stressed that the university respected freedom of expression.
"We do honour and respect individual choice of various opinions and philosophies," he told reporters.
"We reiterate the freedom of expression of the University of Hong Kong by any members including staff and students, as long as we do abide by the university rules and regulations," he said.
The university had agreed to allow the sculpture to be shown on its premises for two weeks, which was the normal duration for similar on-campus exhibitions, Wong said.
But the student leader said the students would fight for a longer display period.

The sculpture was put on display in a Hong Kong park on June 4 for a commemoration of the 1989 Beijing student democracy movement. But Civic authorities had refused to allow the sculpture to remain in public parks after this date.
Democrats have denounced their move as suppressing freedom of speech and expression.
